note: Workstream D0 (plan 2026-10-01 §4): the vertical stack under the flat street datum. Model y 0 = the street the model flattens; beside the river that is Upper Wacker (≈ 599.6 ft NAVD88), in the Loop interior ≈ 593.6 ft, on the lakefront the park / LSD grade (≈ 593 ft). All model values are metres. D1–D5 read these; nothing renders from this file yet. Findings and corrections: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-01-d0-findings.md.

notes.RIVER_Y: Upper Wacker median − river at its regulated normal level (−2.0 ft CCD = 577.31 ft NAVD88) = 6.83 m. −6.3 is the deepest value that keeps the plan's lake step ≤ 1.7 m with LAKE_Y inside tolerance; it equals the river at the top of its regulated band (−0.5 ft CCD → 6.34 m). Plan value −6.0 was 0.83 m short (outside ±0.7).
notes.LAKE_Y: Lakefront street/park median − Lake Michigan long-term mean (578.81 ft IGLD85 → 579.31 ft NAVD88) = 4.28 m. −4.65 keeps the river→lake step at 1.65 m (≤ 1.7). Revetment / harbour-wall / beach-edge / pier-deck tops (lakeEdge) are only ≈ 2.6 m above the lake: D5 aprons step from y 0 down to ≈ LAKE_Y + 2.6, then to the water.
notes.RIVERWALK_Y: Upper Wacker − Riverwalk median = 5.77 m; Riverwalk ≈ 1.0 m above normal pool. Kept exactly 1.0 m over RIVER_Y in the model (−5.3).
notes.LOWER_Y: Where Lower Wacker is open to the sky at its ramp mouths (Lake, Madison, Congress) the 2017 DEM reads 582.6–583.8 ft, median 583.3 ⇒ 5.0 m under the Upper Wacker median (sampleSummary.lowerDropM). From the structure: 13′9″ clearance + 13″ slab + 24″ ribs + ≈ 3″ wearing course ≈ 17.1 ft = 5.2 m. −5.1 m gives 4.2 m clear under a 0.9 m slab.
notes.LOWER2_Y: Lower Lower Wacker / Lower Lower Randolph are covered. Where an upper deck is a mapped bridge (Stetson × South Water) the DEM sees the level under it 4.05 m (13.3 ft) down; Upper → Lower is 5.0–5.2 m. A third level 4.0–4.4 m under LOWER_Y ⇒ −9.5 (plan value kept). In reality this level is ≈ 2.9 m above the river; in the model it sits behind the dockwall, below RIVER_Y.
notes.SLAB_M: Upper Wacker deck: 13 in slab on 2 ft deep × 4 ft wide longitudinal ribs (0.94 m at the ribs, 0.33 m between). 0.9 m.
notes.CLEAR_M: Rebuilt 2001–02 from 12′6″ to at least 13′9″ (4.19 m). Posted truck clearance at the entrances is 13′0″.
notes.levelSpacing: Measured spacing between stacked street levels: 5.0–5.2 m (Upper → Lower Wacker: LiDAR at the open ramp mouths, and clearance + structure), 4.05 m (Upper → Lower South Water / Lower Stetson, LiDAR under a mapped bridge), 4.3 m (Upper Michigan → Upper Wacker at DuSable, LiDAR 613.8 − 599.7 ft).

datum.ccdCalibration: City of Chicago elevation benchmarks (CCD) vs the 2017 1 m DEM at the same coordinates, n = 39 benchmarks between 41.85–41.95 N, 87.60–87.70 W: median NAVD88 − CCD = 579.31 ft (IQR 579.08–579.50); monuments in manholes 579.39. Cross-check: CPL gives 580 ft IGLD85 ≈ 580.5 ft NAVD88 ≈ +1.3 ft CCD ⇒ 579.2. Benchmark #1 (Northern Trust, 50 S LaSalle, primary city bench, 17.64 ft CCD, 3.22 ft above sidewalk) ⇒ sidewalk 14.42 ft CCD = 593.7 ft NAVD88, matching the Loop-street LiDAR median 593.6.
datum.ccdHistoric: CCD 0 = 579.88 ft above mean tide at New York (the NGVD-era figure the plan quoted). It is NOT the NAVD88 value; use ccdZeroNavd88Ft.
datum.igldNote: CPL: lake at 580 ft IGLD85 ≈ 580.5 ft NAVD88 at Chicago.

water.riverNote: 33 CFR 207.420 / MWRD: the river at the Chicago River Controlling Works is held between −0.5 and −2.0 ft CCD, normally −2.0 ft.
water.lakeNote: Lake Michigan–Huron: 1918–2016 mean 578.81 ft IGLD85; June 2017 monthly mean 176.88 m = 580.31 ft (the LiDAR month); chart datum (LWD) 577.5 ft; record monthly high 582.35 ft (October 1986; 2020 came within ≈ 0.1 ft).
water.lockNote: Chicago Harbor Lock: normal lift 2.0 ft; cycles 2–5 ft differences. Lake mean (579.31 NAVD88) − river normal (577.31) = 2.0 ft = 0.61 m: the real step at the lock.
water.lidarWaterNote: The 2017 DEM is hydro-flattened: the river AND the nearshore lake both read 576.09–576.10 ft, offshore 574.83 ft. Those are breakline artefacts (the lake was 580.8 ft NAVD88 that month), so water surfaces come from the regulation and gauge data above, never from the DEM.
